title: Drop-In Masked Modular Reduction for ML-DSA: Cutting Side-Channel Cost in the Root-of-Trust
evidence_span: The first-order masked ML-DSA modular-reduction design for the Caliptra root of trust reports 12.1x speedup, 86.7% fewer LUTs, 94.5% fewer FFs, 91x area-delay-efficiency improvement, and 1.32x signing throughput; TVLA over more than one million traces reports no first-order leakage.
problem: First-order masking for post-quantum ML-DSA protects against side channels but imposes roughly 6x area overhead in constrained root-of-trust hardware.
method_or_artifact: Drop-in masked modular-reduction architecture optimized for Caliptra ML-DSA signing.
workload_or_benchmark: Caliptra ML-DSA reduction and signing with TVLA leakage evaluation over more than one million traces; FPGA/ASIC process, clock, security order, and baseline implementation details are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Caliptra root-of-trust hardware with masked ML-DSA, LUT/FF resource accounting, and first-order TVLA; target fabric/process, voltage, and area boundary are unspecified.
metrics: No first-order leakage in TVLA over more than 1,000,000 traces
limits: The description omits absolute area, delay, power, TVLA setup, leakage threshold, higher-order leakage, and process details.
No first-order leakage under the reported test does not establish security against higher-order or implementation-specific attacks.
Official description only; cryptographic and hardware claims require paper-level verification.

title: Detrojan: Detecting Trojan Circuits Using a Purpose-Built Graph Neural Network with Community-Enhanced Classification
evidence_span: DeTrojan combines functionality-aware features, edge-aware GNN layers with jumping knowledge/global context, and community-aware localization refinement; on 2025 ICCAD CAD Contest hardware-Trojan benchmarks it reports 16.7% better circuit-level accuracy and 47.3% relative gate-level F1 improvement over state-of-the-art ML methods.
problem: Structure-only GNN features and fragmented node predictions limit gate-level hardware-Trojan detection accuracy and localization.
method_or_artifact: Functionality-aware feature engineering, edge-aware GNN with global context, and community-aware classification refinement.
workload_or_benchmark: 2025 ICCAD CAD Contest hardware-Trojan benchmarks; circuit counts, Trojan families, splits, class imbalance, and baseline implementations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Gate-level netlist graphs for hardware-Trojan detection; synthesis/library provenance, design scale, and deployment context are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 16.6% accuracy gain and 2x F1 gain when modules augment existing approaches
limits: The description omits absolute scores, false-positive cost, unseen-Trojan generalization, dataset leakage controls, and runtime.
Contest benchmarks may not represent proprietary netlists or adaptive attackers.
Official description only; security-detection claims require dataset and adversarial validation.

title: Shortcircuit: Alphazero-Driven Generative Circuit Design
evidence_span: ShortCircuit generates AND-Inverter Graphs from truth tables with a transformer trained by supervised learning and an AlphaZero variant; on 500 eight-input truth tables from real circuits it guarantees functional correctness, outperforms ABC in circuit size, and uses greedy rollout for a reported 31x speedup.
problem: Traditional logic-synthesis heuristics have plateaued, while direct learning over the doubly exponential circuit state space is difficult.
method_or_artifact: Transformer-based AIG generator with supervised pretraining and AlphaZero search, plus greedy rollout acceleration.
workload_or_benchmark: 500 eight-input truth tables derived from real circuits, compared with ABC; circuit-size definition, timing/power constraints, training/test split, and ABC version are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Boolean AIG synthesis from truth tables; target technology mapping, library, optimization objectives, and inference hardware are unspecified.
metrics: Functional correctness guaranteed for generated circuits claimed
limits: The description omits exact circuit-size results, timing/area/power tradeoffs, generalization beyond eight inputs, and search/training cost.
Functional correctness does not imply PPA superiority after technology mapping.
Official description only; synthesis and learning claims require paper-level artifact verification.

title: BREW-RC: Bit-Exact Recovery of ECCs from Write Timing in ReRAM Crossbars
evidence_span: BREW-RC infers ReRAM ECC parity matrices from write-latency variation, encodes timing perturbations as a SAT instance, and demonstrates complete ECC recovery from multiple samples of two commercial ReRAM products.
problem: ECC parity bits in ReRAM crossbars are not directly readable, limiting reliability characterization and timing-side-channel modeling.
method_or_artifact: Non-invasive write-timing side-channel analysis with SAT-based recovery of the bit-exact ECC parity matrix.
workload_or_benchmark: Two commercial ReRAM products and multiple device samples; write patterns, timing resolution, ECC families, measurement equipment, and recovery success rates are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Commercial ReRAM crossbar memories with hidden ECC and variable write latency; controller, process, environmental, interface, and attacker-access assumptions are unspecified.
baselines: opaque ECC behavior without recovered parity matrix
timing models that omit ECC parity effects
metrics: Complete ECC recovery on two commercial ReRAM products
limits: The description omits sample complexity, measurement noise, recovery time, countermeasures, and product diversity.
Recovery feasibility may depend on physical access and stable timing conditions not present in deployed systems.
Official description only; side-channel and reliability implications require paper-level verification.

title: STAMP: Semiconductor Tool-Chain Attestation Through Wafer-Level Machine Learning-Based Process Monitoring
evidence_span: STAMP uses systematic process variation and causal relationships between tool exchanges and silicon dimensions/electrical characteristics to distinguish sanctioned from unsanctioned manufacturing tool chains; it is demonstrated on inline and e-test measurements from 7,000 wafers with multiple tool-chain variants in GlobalFoundries 12LP FinFET.
problem: Manufacturing organizations need wafer-level evidence that a sanctioned or ratified semiconductor tool chain produced the silicon, despite subtle process-variation signatures.
method_or_artifact: Machine-learning process-monitoring model for wafer-level tool-chain attestation using metrology and wafer-acceptance-test measurements.
workload_or_benchmark: 7,000 wafers, multiple tool-chain variants, inline and e-test measurements, GlobalFoundries 12LP FinFET; accuracy, splits, tool variants, and attack model are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 12LP FinFET manufacturing flow with inline metrology and electrical testing; foundry process, measurement cadence, model features, and chain-of-custody controls are unspecified.
baselines: ordinary process monitoring without tool-chain attestation
sanctioned versus unsanctioned tool-chain classification baselines
limits: The description omits classification accuracy, false-accept/reject rates, temporal holdout, process drift, and adversarial adaptation.
A single technology node and foundry dataset may not generalize to other fabs, nodes, or tool substitutions.
Official description only; supply-chain attestation claims require paper-level and operational validation.
